Definition: from G4314 and ὤψ (the visage, from G3700); the front (as being towards view), i.e. the countenance, aspect, appearance, surface; by implication, presence, person:--(outward) appearance, X before, countenance, face, fashion, (men's) person, presence.
BiblicalUsage: Prosopon is the face, the countenance, the front of a person, and by extension the presence itself. Moses' face shone, and Paul says we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image. God has shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ. On the mount, Jesus' face did shine as the sun, and in the New Jerusalem His servants shall see His face.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the face is where glory lives: Moses caught it secondhand and shone, and we behold it in Christ and are changed. I hold that seeing His face is the end of the whole story, because the beatitude of the pure in heart was always this, that they shall see God.
